header.running_head: The Enthusiasm of the Sahabah (RA) to Die and Give their Lives in the path of Allaah

blocks.text: The Incident of Hadhrat Umar (RA) and his brother Zaid (RA) Concerning not Wearing Armour with the Intention of being Martyred

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that on the day that the Battle of Uhud was fought, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to his brother, "Take my armour, dear brother." His brother replied, "I desire martyrdom just as you do." They both therefore left the armour.[^1]
Hadhrat Ali (RA) Resolves to Fight to Death

Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Mansoor reports that Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Once the people had left Rasulullaah ﷺ during the Battle of Uhud, I looked through all the dead and did not see Rasulullaah ﷺ there. I then said to myself, 'By Allaah! It is impossible for Rasulullaah ﷺ to flee and I do not see him amongst the dead. I think that Allaah has become angry with us because of what we did and had lifted his Nabi ﷺ. It is therefore best for me to fight until I am killed.' I then broke the sheath of my sword and attacked the Mushrikeen. When they gave way, I suddenly saw Rasulullaah ﷺ in their midst."[^2]
The Incident of Hadhrat Anas bin Nadhar (RA)

Hadhrat Qaasim bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Raafi (RA) who belonged to the Banu Adi bin Najjaar tribe narrates that Hadhrat Anas bin Nadhar (RA) the uncle of Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) came across some men from the Muhaajireen and the Ansaar (during the Battle of Uhud) who had lost all morale to fight. Amongst them was Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) and Hadhrat Talha bin Ubaydillaah (RA). Hadhrat Anas bin Nadhar (RA) asked them, "What makes you sit here?" "Rasulullaah ﷺ has been martyred," they replied. He then said to them, "What is the use of living after him? Stand up and die for that which Rasulullaah ﷺ died for!" He then faced the enemy and fought until he was killed.[^3]
blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Qaasim bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Raafi (RA)

blocks.text: The Incident of Hadhrat Thaabit bin Dahdaaha (RA)

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ammaar Khatmi (RA) reports that Hadhrat Thaabit bin Dahdaaha (RA) came before the Muslims during the Battle of Uhud when they were all scattered and without morale. He shouted, "O assembly of Ansaar! Come to me! Come to me! I am Thaabit bin Dahdaaha! If Muhammad ﷺ has been killed, remember that Allaah is Living and never dies. Fight for your Deen, Allaah shall give you victory and shall assist you." A group of the Ansaar jumped towards him and Hadhrat Thaabit (RA) started attacking the Kuffaar with the Muslims by his side.
A fully armed and powerful battalion stood before them comprising of leading
Tabraani narrating from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.5 Pg.298). Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.275) and Abu Nu'aym in Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.367) have also reported the narration.
Abu Ya'la, Ibn Abi Aasim, Boraqi and Sa'eed bin Mansoor, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.274). Haythami (Vol.6 Pg.112) has commented on the chain of narrators.
Ibn Is'haaq, as quoted in Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.4 Pg.34).
